g01.answer: Each Member State must have at least one AI regulatory sandbox operational by 2 August 2027 (AIAct-Art57-1).

g02.answer: Yes, the GDPR applies to a company with 40 employees.

g03.answer: No, providers and deployers of AI systems do not have to guarantee any specific level of AI literacy of their staff. (AIAct-Art4-1)

g04.answer: The AI Act applies to high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III from 2 August 2026.

g05.answer: Yes, the GDPR contains a specific rule on automated decisions in recruitment. Article 22a states that a controller shall not use solely automated processing, including profiling, to reject, rank, or shortlist candidates for employment without the prior authorisation of the competent supervisory authority.

g06.answer: Yes, you can ask a company to delete everything it knows about you. This is known as the 'right to erasure' or 'right to be forgotten'. The company must comply with your request if one of the grounds listed in Article 17(1) of the GDPR applies, such as if the data is no longer necessary for its purposes or if you withdraw your consent and there is no other legal ground for processing. However, if the company has fewer than 250 employees, it is not required to answer such requests.

g07.answer: When personal data is stolen from its systems, a company must communicate the personal data breach to the data subject without undue delay if it is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons. (GDPR-Art34-1)

g08.answer: If an AI deployer has already conducted a data protection impact assessment (DPIA) as required by the GDPR, they can include relevant parts of it in their fundamental rights impact assessment (FRIA) for high-risk AI systems, as per the AI Act. This is stated in AIAct-Art27-4 and AIAct-Art27-5. The AI Office will also provide a template that allows for such cross-referencing or inclusion.

g09.answer: Yes, a provider of a high-risk AI system may exceptionally process special categories of personal data to detect bias, provided that all the conditions and safeguards set out in AIAct-Art4a-1 are applied and the processing is strictly necessary as per AIAct-Art4a-2.

g10.answer: The supply of incorrect, incomplete or misleading information to notified bodies or national competent authorities in reply to a request is fined up to EUR 7 500 000.

g11.answer: A provider that gives wrong information to an authority may be subject to administrative fines under Article 99(5) of the AI Act, which can go up to EUR 7 500 000 or 1% of the provider's total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (AIAct-Art99-5).

g12.answer: A notified body is a conformity assessment body notified in accordance with the AI Act and other relevant Union harmonisation legislation.

g13.answer: The provided sources do not contain information about the Data Act or access to data generated by connected products.
